tip: An ett-word normally makes the definite by adding '-et': 'smör' becomes 'smöret' (the butter).
The preposition stays at the end here: 'att välja på' means to choose from.
'Med tanke på' is a set phrase meaning considering or in view of: 'med tanke på vädret'.
'Hem' = homeward (motion); 'hemma' = at home (location): 'hem gick vi' = home we went.
'Man' means a generic you or one: 'hur säger man' is how do you say.
The whole clause 'hur vi löser problemet' fills the first slot, so the main verb comes next, before its subject: 'vet jag inte'.
'Bli' means become, used for future states: 'det ska bli spännande' = it will be exciting.
A definite ett-word with an adjective marks twice: 'det' before it, and 'vattnet' keeps its '-et' ending.
'Som' is the usual relative word for both people and things: 'pojken som bor' (the boy who lives).
Front a negative adverb like 'sällan' and the verb comes before the subject: 'ser man'.
'Så fort' means as soon as. After that clause the main verb comes before its subject: 'somnade jag'.
'Så fort' means as soon as; the clause it opens comes first, then the main verb comes before the subject: 'kliver vi'.
'Varje' means every, and takes a singular noun: 'varje morgon' = every morning.
Paired comparison: 'ju mer' in the first half, then 'desto' plus the comparative in the second: 'desto bättre'.
State your name with 'heter' (am called), not the verb for to be: 'jag heter Anna'.
'Förra' = last/previous for time periods: 'förra våren' = last spring.
Days of the week take 'på': 'på lördag' means on Saturday.
'Bra' means both good and well and never adds '-t': 'dansar bra' stays 'bra'.
'Detsamma' means likewise, used to return a greeting or good wish: same to you.
Add '-s' to a past verb to make it passive: 'hittades' means was found, with no separate word for was.
Turn an adjective into an adverb by adding '-t': 'vacker' becomes 'vackert' (beautifully) in 'sjöng vackert'.
Adjectives describing a plural noun take '-a': 'dagarna' are 'korta och mörka'.
'Vore' means would be, the conditional form of 'vara': 'det bästa vore' (the best would be).
'Hela' (whole) sits before an already-definite noun with no extra article: 'hela sjön', not 'en hel sjö'.
'En annan femma' = a different five (coin) – a whole different story.
'Stiga' is a strong verb, so its past changes the vowel instead of adding an ending: 'steg' (rose).
Yes or no questions put the verb first, before the subject: 'har ni'.
Regular '-a' verbs form the past with '-ade': 'skörda' becomes 'skördade' (harvested).
Possession just adds '-s', with no apostrophe: 'ugglans rop' means the owl's call.
Add '-s' for possession, even on definite nouns: 'landets ekonomi' = the country's economy.
